supersedes.preservation: The original rejection and binary-contamination evidence remain byte-for-byte unchanged. This record replaces only its conclusion after rerunning against immutable per-commit binaries.

verdict_reason: The Rust implementation is a direct behavioral match for Java DotPath.moveStartPoint, including equality consumption, the size-greater-than-one guard, at-most-one removal with three cubics, residual vector subtraction, coincident-control fallback, and fully degenerate first-cubic behavior. Six of eight fresh valid PlantUML perturbations pass diff_one structurally. The two nonzero fresh diffs preserve the target route's segment count and retraction geometry and expose already-separate global-frame translation or relationship-ID/subpixel serialization residue. No source-level or executable model counterexample was found, and immutable binary hashes remained constant before and after every run.

source_trace_findings.finding: For SIMPLIER links, Java derives the start angle from DotPath, creates the decoration, and moves the path start by the decoration's provenance-owned length along that angle.

Java consumes only when more than one cubic exists and movement magnitude is greater than or equal to the first endpoint chord. It removes exactly one cubic, subtracts the vector between the first and second cubic starts, and applies the residual to the surviving start and first control.

The tangent uses first-control displacement with first-endpoint fallback, while the threshold is endpoint chord length. A fully degenerate tangent reaches atan2(0,0), yielding Java's zero-angle positive-x movement.

source_trace_findings.location: Rust crates/rustuml-render/src/class.rs shortened_endpoint_points and dotpath_start_unit_tangent at e8d50060
source_trace_findings.finding: The Rust point stream uses one start followed by triples per cubic. len >= 7 is exactly Java's more-than-one-cubic guard; draining the first three entries removes exactly one cubic while retaining its endpoint as the surviving start. shift minus first_chord is Java's residual vector, and the control/endpoint/positive-x tangent fallbacks match Java.

results: equal-two: a movement exactly equal to the 4px chord consumes the first cubic
below-two: 3.999px does not consume the 4px chord
single-large: an 8px movement cannot consume the only cubic
three-large-consumes-one: a 20px movement leaves two of three cubics, proving at-most-one removal
oblique-residual: the residual is vector subtraction, not scalar subtraction along the surviving chord
control-at-endpoint: a noncoincident first control remains the tangent even when it equals the endpoint
fully-degenerate-first: Java consumes the zero-length first cubic and applies positive-x movement
